entries.search: This meeting place in the abandoned mines is associated with the imprisoned Lu-a-Jalla. Her rescue turns the search for the Princess into the search for her beloved At-Zako and opens the next stage of Zak’s journey. The former punishment cell is empty. Zak follows the trail deeper into the Forbidden Catacombs until he finds [[character/deva]], who first mistakes him for another captor. She has escaped the mercenaries and found protection through the ancient treaty between Joons and Wormheads. She rejects the nickname Princess and explains that Diera imprisoned her out of jealousy over the governor. Zak falls in love with her, but she remains faithful to At-Zako, who drew the Joon Curse away from her. Zak promises to respect that bond. They return to Tka-Rik, and the next mission becomes the search for her missing beloved on Suslanger.

entries.search: The arrow in the Snoop’s body appears to implicate the Woodsfolk. Sver explains that their markings identify a clan, while the governor discovers that the case containing similar arrows has been stolen from his collection. Two lines of inquiry now run alongside each other: the stolen collection and the Woodsfolk’s testimony. To approach [[character/ycf]], Zak first returns the Green Clan’s Sacred Flower after rescuing its keeper from the White Clan. Grey Leaf then asks for help with the kidnapped elder Khabburu and his captor. The clan ultimately identifies the murder arrow as a false attribution, even refusing to blame its enemies for it. When the clan moves, Zak receives access to its hidden route and new home. [[character/shopper]] first lets Baldie’s name slip while boasting that mechanical traps are better than magical ones, then denies knowing anything useful. Tilvar mentions the merchant’s mechanical grinder and the disruption caused when it breaks. Sver knows how to turn these leads into pressure. Zak first delivers the hunter’s furs to a buyer outside the merchant’s monopoly. Sver then reveals Karansul’s hidden trade and unpaid taxes, pointing to the foreman’s accounts; he also recommends [[character/mthief]] as a teacher. With the accounts as leverage, Zak learns where to find [[character/vor]], called Baldie, and secures a meeting. Evidence from the stolen collection makes the thief confess: he killed the Snoop, planted the Woodsfolk arrow and worked for a cloaked employer who knew how to evade the governor’s magical traps. At the Green Clan’s new home, Grey Leaf describes the supposed man in grey as a white-haired woman. Zak identifies Diera, whose own traps protected the stolen collection. Her urgent warnings against the abandoned mines reinforce his suspicion. Tilvar explains that the governor holds the key. Karansul suggests winning it with a gold nugget and gives access to a dangerous pit, concealing the tigers that drove out its workers; Sver warns Zak of the trap. Zak obtains the nugget and presents it to the collector-governor as a business prospect. Valrasian releases the mine key, opening the way past Diera’s mercenaries.

entries.search: [[character/daughter]] is Estera’s strong-willed granddaughter. Determined to be taken seriously by Zak and her grandmother, she investigates the way into the Dead City and explains how a lizard’s amulet can lead a dragon against the harpies at the observatory. Her attempt to find the magician places her in danger, and Zak’s search for her becomes part of his dealings with [[character/orcc]]. Before Estera’s formal introduction, Zak can meet Airy at the cave; she warns him about her grandmother and the traps protecting their home. [[character/witch]] initially threatens the intruder, then changes her reception when Zak offers the Magic Bit. She dismisses the villagers’ divine-saviour story but discovers that she cannot see his past. Since Zak cannot remember it either, she suggests finding the orcs’ Magic Orb and directs him back to Erfar for information. This is the beginning of their alliance. Estera also introduces her granddaughter [[character/daughter]], warning Zak to keep his distance; Airy resents being treated as a child. Zak’s search now has a personal aim beyond the village’s demands. When Estera uses the Orb, Zak sees an old man instead of a recognisable memory. She believes he is its owner and a more powerful magician who might help. Orc records trace the object to the Dead City. Estera distinguishes its human fortress from Gipath’s much older ruins: after the Night of Troubles, the dead attacked the living, and survivors fled to found the present village. The obvious route into the fortress is deadly. Airy leaves to investigate another way in, despite her grandmother’s objections. Separately, Erfar can send Zak into the surrounding region’s Golden Valley for a caravan’s lost treasure, an errand he badly understates. Airy returns with a lead to the old observatory library, but harpies occupy the site. Her plan requires a lizard’s amulet to lead a particular green dragon against them. Reaching that dragon requires Estera to freeze the lake with a green crystal. The hostile lizards on the approach present another obstacle: Zak moves the Big Shell from the Remote Mountains to the Middle Mountains, restoring the peace associated with its altar. This leaves Babur’s former quarry route unsafe and can lead to an additional errand for the craftsman. The observatory book finally supplies the password to the Dead City’s hidden entrance. Airy can also teach Zak the Magic of Feelings, only to be offended when he again calls her a little girl. Before leaving Gipath, Zak can finish the separate search for Airy, who set out to find the magician herself and impress him. Estera’s vision points to a goblin prison, where Zak finds her granddaughter’s potion bottle and a note leading to [[character/orcc]]. The orc chief intends to give Airy to a frightening armoured human he calls a Demon. Zak offers to remove this threat instead. Shei-Var first demands proof of his strength against the ogre brothers, whose wealth also threatens the chief’s influence. Once Zak defeats the Demon, Shei-Var honours his promise and sends Airy home. The rescue ends with Estera’s gratitude and Airy’s distress that Zak still regards her as a child.

entries.search: [[character/iz]] is the Khadaganian officer to whom Kardaur brings Zak. He treats the prisoner as material for training his soldiers in Death Canyon. His threat to make Kardaur take Zak’s place if the captive dies too quickly shows that his cruelty also extends to his subordinates. Zak is captured near the portal on [[allod/suslanger]]. Lieutenant [[character/karh]] presents him to [[character/iz]], who orders him used as live quarry for soldiers seeking promotion. Surviving the run through Death Canyon earns only a return to captivity, not freedom. Kardaur threatens punishment through necromancy if Zak dies too quickly and displeases his superior.

entries.search: [[character/smith]] is the village craftsman. The theft of his favourite tools leaves him unable to work, and their recovery wins Zak access to his services. He distrusts Erfar’s “Free Hunters”, bargains fiercely and knows much about the surrounding ruins. His advice about the Magic Bit, the drawbridge mechanism and Estera’s trap key helps Zak reach the witch. Killing the sentry brings another request from Erfar: the White Wolf and its pack are taking the village livestock. After Zak kills their leader, Erfar and Gort press him to surrender the head so the captain can claim prestige. Gort also sends him to punish the goblins while the village soldiers stay home. Meanwhile [[character/smith]] refuses to work until his stolen iron tools are returned. Erfar calls the thieves friendly “Free Hunters”; Babur calls them brigands and describes the beating of his apprentice. Recovering the chisel and bodkin from the chief and his wife wins Zak the craftsman’s services. These early errands expose the disagreement between the village’s leaders and the man who equips it. Babur’s account of a red-haired brigand meeting orcs gives Zak his next lead. A map taken from Redhead points to a Magic Bit in a sarcophagus in the orc cave. Babur explains that Estera values such objects, while Gort can supply the missing drawbridge mechanism. Zak obtains the seer’s key and the object, then asks how to reach the witch. Babur, who made her spare trap key, explains the guarded ravines and controlling obelisks. The craftsman expects a share of the sale. Zak instead intends to exchange the find for help with his lost memory. Babur also offers a separate reward for weakening the orcs in the Foothills. Their seer controls an ancient pyramid that strikes intruders with lightning. If Zak accepts, he kills the seer and shuts the device down, allowing the craftsman to travel more safely. When Babur pays him, Zak asks why a land without a king uses royal coins. Babur explains that the money survives from an earlier civilisation. Accessible ruins have already been stripped; richer finds lie in places dangerous enough to discourage even him. GoGo’s presence in the village exposes competing interests. Gort silences the chief under Erfar’s orders and refuses to let Zak question him without the elder. Babur, meanwhile, recognises the Eye Stone as a valuable meteorite. He proposes killing GoGo and dividing the proceeds. Zak rejects the suggestion, making clear that his dealings with the craftsman do not amount to accepting every scheme he offers. Erfar links the missing village taxes to the disappearance of Babur’s apprentice and accuses the craftsman of plotting to take power. Babur denies the charge: he suspects the brigands of stealing the gold and kidnapping his worker. Erfar proposes replacing the money with treasure from a ruined caravan in Golden Valley. Babur exposes the danger omitted from this offer: earlier visitors vanished, and one survivor returned deranged, speaking of undead guards. Zak can refuse the expedition. Erfar then reproaches him and later claims another man supplied the gold. If Zak instead retrieves it, the elder thanks him with promises of a song and admits that he understated the danger. Neither exchange establishes what actually happened to the apprentice. While Zak seeks the magician, Erfar and Gort arrange another joint operation with the Free Hunters, supposedly to prevent a goblin raid. The promised friendly meeting becomes an ambush by brigands and village soldiers. Erfar denies responsibility. Gort blames drunken, undisciplined soldiers and brigands dressed as villagers, then briefly threatens to overthrow Erfar before withdrawing the threat. Babur warns that the elder is trying to have Zak killed. A note in the newer orc script cannot yet settle the matter: Estera needs an Orc ABC Book to read it. Its translation reveals a contract on Zak’s life, a detailed description of him and a substantial payment. The search for the author becomes a separate investigation alongside the route into the Dead City. Airy returns with a lead to the old observatory library, but harpies occupy the site. Her plan requires a lizard’s amulet to lead a particular green dragon against them. Reaching that dragon requires Estera to freeze the lake with a green crystal. The hostile lizards on the approach present another obstacle: Zak moves the Big Shell from the Remote Mountains to the Middle Mountains, restoring the peace associated with its altar. This leaves Babur’s former quarry route unsafe and can lead to an additional errand for the craftsman. The observatory book finally supplies the password to the Dead City’s hidden entrance. Airy can also teach Zak the Magic of Feelings, only to be offended when he again calls her a little girl. Moving the Big Shell solves one problem and creates another. Babur can no longer use the road protected by its old altar. The alternative route passes a cyclops tending pigs stolen from the village, and the craftsman offers payment to make it safe. Zak can kill the cyclops or destroy its food supply and wait for it to leave. The latter plan depends on remaining unnoticed. Babur pays once access is restored. The dispute shows why his advice about the Shell serves his own livelihood as well as Zak’s journey. After Gort’s fall, Erfar claims that an orc seer has cursed the village with disease and asks for a White Flower. Babur wants to monopolise the healing flower and charge Erfar ruinous prices; Zak rebukes him. Zak finds armed opposition waiting for him, although no villagers have yet fallen ill. Erfar blames Babur, while Babur’s earlier warning makes Zak suspect both men. Estera suggests setting a trap. Zak tells each suspect a different location for a second flower; the ambush appears at the place he gave Erfar. With Rivar’s support he confronts and imprisons the elder. An expedition report recovered from the abandoned foreign camp becomes leverage: Erfar translates its account of a concealed tunnel and its opening lever. He later escapes custody. Estera recalls that he originally arrived as an adult stranger, leaving his real purpose unresolved. Babur welcomes the exposure and says that the villagers feared Erfar rather than loved him.

entries.search: Brissen is a knight allied with the Woodsfolk who describes his life as service to good. He offers to accompany Zak after hearing of him from Grey Leaf. His methods are less gentle than his ideals sound: he explains how the Woodsfolk intimidate witnesses who might recognise him in the city. Brissen is alive when Zak meets him, despite rumours in the city. Grey Leaf has told him about Zak, and he offers to serve the good cause alongside him. His professed ideals do not forbid stealth or rough methods; he says that war against evil requires practical means. Duties defending the Woodsfolk against the Black Clan can delay his departure. After being recognised, he can hide with the Green Clan. He explains that Grey Leaf keeps his presence secret by threatening witnesses with the burning or collapse of their property until they dismiss the sighting as a drunken dream. His farewell again dismisses rumours of his death.

entries.search: [[character/kuzn]] finds Zak after his escape through the caves and speaks for him before Khatul. After his smithy burned down, he fled before his debt could lead to enslavement and maintains secret trade with city merchants to equip the Shelter. He asks Zak to settle an old grievance against the slavedriver brothers Lash-Aga and Whip-Aga, a request that brings him into conflict with Khatul’s caution. Beyond the caves, [[character/kuzn]] finds Zak and vouches for him before [[character/glav]]. The brotherhood’s leader fears imperial spies and requires the Emperor’s Signet Ring, taken from a cyclops who killed its courier. Possessing such an object compromises the newcomer with the authorities and makes the test more than a feat of strength. After Zak returns, Khatul accepts him as Brother Blondie and offers the refuge as a new home. Zak explains his promise to find At-Zako and return to Gipath. Khatul respects that purpose and asks those who can help to support him; [[character/guru]] can teach him greater dexterity. The Shelter’s inhabitants can ask for help with their own grievances alongside the search for At-Zako. Brother Blacksmith wants the slavedriver brothers Lash-Aga and Whip-Aga killed at the plantations. If Zak carries out the request, the workers raise the alarm instead of helping him. The smith explains that imperial law threatens them with death if they fail to report a stranger, then promises to repay the revenge. Kehel offers a separate commission: destroy a harpy he once experimented on, so rivals cannot claim his work. After its death, he admits that fear of Zak’s strength is what makes him honour the promised reward. Their requests expose different consequences of life under the empire: coerced obedience among the workers, personal revenge among its fugitives, and rivalry among its scholars. [[character/merc10]] supplies the next lead through her own theft. Antiquities she stole from [[character/junofil]] remain hidden near the city, and Zak recovers them to arrange a meeting. Khatul and Brother Blacksmith help choose the secluded trading place, keeping strangers away from the Shelter. entries.search: [[character/zaku]] appears among the brothers of the Last Shelter, claiming to hide a face disfigured by torture. Khatul trusts him to guide Zak toward the Portal. This identity is a disguise: at their later meeting the former village elder [[character/elder]] reveals himself and explains how he has arranged for the guards to intercept Zak. Khatul asks [[character/zaku]] to help Zak reach the guarded portal. Faceless arranges a cave meeting and explains the keys and stone controls. He then reveals himself as Erfar: born on Suslanger, he went to Gipath seeking the meteorite and manipulated the villagers into searching for it. His earlier plots were attempts to remove Zak, who disrupted that scheme. The reunion is another trap, with guards waiting outside the cave. Zak survives the confrontation and forces a route through the portal’s defences. Activating its two controls finally returns him to Tka-Rik with the amulet fragments.

entries.search: The hurried transformation that concealed At-Zako nearly destroyed his memory. Tka-Rik cannot safely repeat it, so hiding as Zak is no longer an answer. He offers another choice: flee again under his temporary protection, or confront the Curse on Gipath. At-Zako chooses to defend his life with Lu-a-Jalla. entries.search: Babur’s account of a red-haired brigand meeting orcs gives Zak his next lead. A map taken from Redhead points to a Magic Bit in a sarcophagus in the orc cave. Babur explains that Estera values such objects, while Gort can supply the missing drawbridge mechanism. Zak obtains the seer’s key and the object, then asks how to reach the witch. Babur, who made her spare trap key, explains the guarded ravines and controlling obelisks. The craftsman expects a share of the sale. Zak instead intends to exchange the find for help with his lost memory. The observatory’s password takes Zak into the Dead City and up Lone Mountain. He expects the magician from the Orb but finds [[character/skd]]. The dragon insists on an old bargain: a visitor must perform a task before receiving an answer. Zak deals with the armadillos beneath the lair, using the poison the dragon supplies. The dragon then admits that he cannot identify Zak or locate Gipath’s elusive Great Magician. He suggests the ancient lizards might know more and points instead to an expedition of armoured outsiders. He withdraws the skeletons he had used against their camp. In a further conversation, he gives Zak an old sword because he enjoys his company and would rather not see him become another speechless skeleton.

entries.search: This cave meeting exposes the Faceless Brother’s identity. Erfar tells Zak about his past on Suslanger, his meteorite scheme and the ambush he has arranged. It closes the village conspiracy’s thread far from the village itself. Khatul asks [[character/zaku]] to help Zak reach the guarded portal. Faceless arranges a cave meeting and explains the keys and stone controls. He then reveals himself as Erfar: born on Suslanger, he went to Gipath seeking the meteorite and manipulated the villagers into searching for it. His earlier plots were attempts to remove Zak, who disrupted that scheme. The reunion is another trap, with guards waiting outside the cave. Zak survives the confrontation and forces a route through the portal’s defences. Activating its two controls finally returns him to Tka-Rik with the amulet fragments.

entries.search: On [[allod/ingos]], Zak first crosses the hostile countryside to reach the city. [[character/kapitan]] tells him about the missing young woman known locally as the Princess and the reward offered for finding her. Governor [[character/huber]] takes a personal interest in her, while [[character/magess]] discourages the search. The hunter [[character/trapper]] provides a concrete lead: another investigator, the Snoop from the capital, had followed the same trail before disappearing east of the city. Finding his body changes the search for a missing girl into an investigation of murder. The arrow in the Snoop’s body appears to implicate the Woodsfolk. Sver explains that their markings identify a clan, while the governor discovers that the case containing similar arrows has been stolen from his collection. Two lines of inquiry now run alongside each other: the stolen collection and the Woodsfolk’s testimony. To approach [[character/ycf]], Zak first returns the Green Clan’s Sacred Flower after rescuing its keeper from the White Clan. Grey Leaf then asks for help with the kidnapped elder Khabburu and his captor. The clan ultimately identifies the murder arrow as a false attribution, even refusing to blame its enemies for it. When the clan moves, Zak receives access to its hidden route and new home.

entries.search: When Estera uses the Orb, Zak sees an old man instead of a recognisable memory. She believes he is its owner and a more powerful magician who might help. Orc records trace the object to the Dead City. entries.search: Zak is captured near the portal on [[allod/suslanger]]. Lieutenant [[character/karh]] presents him to [[character/iz]], who orders him used as live quarry for soldiers seeking promotion. Surviving the run through Death Canyon earns only a return to captivity, not freedom. Kardaur threatens punishment through necromancy if Zak dies too quickly and displeases his superior. The [[character/nalo]] approaches Zak after his ordeal. Enslaved by Kardaur and deprived even of a personal name, she wants his death and knows he will guard the gate that night. She steals the key to Zak’s cage. Her father, a rat hunter who disappeared in the caves, told her of the Wormheads’ temple and the bridges across its lava rivers. She uses that knowledge to explain a route the guards fear to follow. Zak kills Kardaur for the fortress key and escapes toward the cave; releasing the caged spiders can delay pursuit. The Odalisque and Zak part with wishes for each other’s freedom and survival, without a stated account of her later fate.

Afterwards Zak learns that this is Gipath’s only human village, with no king or known route to other lands. Killing the sentry brings another request from Erfar: the White Wolf and its pack are taking the village livestock. After Zak kills their leader, Erfar and Gort press him to surrender the head so the captain can claim prestige. Gort also sends him to punish the goblins while the village soldiers stay home. Meanwhile [[character/smith]] refuses to work until his stolen iron tools are returned. Erfar calls the thieves friendly “Free Hunters”; Babur calls them brigands and describes the beating of his apprentice. Recovering the chisel and bodkin from the chief and his wife wins Zak the craftsman’s services. These early errands expose the disagreement between the village’s leaders and the man who equips it. Babur’s account of a red-haired brigand meeting orcs gives Zak his next lead. A map taken from Redhead points to a Magic Bit in a sarcophagus in the orc cave. Babur explains that Estera values such objects, while Gort can supply the missing drawbridge mechanism. Zak obtains the seer’s key and the object, then asks how to reach the witch. Babur, who made her spare trap key, explains the guarded ravines and controlling obelisks. The craftsman expects a share of the sale. Zak instead intends to exchange the find for help with his lost memory. GoGo’s presence in the village exposes competing interests. Gort silences the chief under Erfar’s orders and refuses to let Zak question him without the elder. Babur, meanwhile, recognises the Eye Stone as a valuable meteorite. He proposes killing GoGo and dividing the proceeds. Zak rejects the suggestion, making clear that his dealings with the craftsman do not amount to accepting every scheme he offers. While Zak seeks the magician, Erfar and Gort arrange another joint operation with the Free Hunters, supposedly to prevent a goblin raid. The promised friendly meeting becomes an ambush by brigands and village soldiers. Erfar denies responsibility. Gort blames drunken, undisciplined soldiers and brigands dressed as villagers, then briefly threatens to overthrow Erfar before withdrawing the threat. Babur warns that the elder is trying to have Zak killed. A note in the newer orc script cannot yet settle the matter: Estera needs an Orc ABC Book to read it. Its translation reveals a contract on Zak’s life, a detailed description of him and a substantial payment. The search for the author becomes a separate investigation alongside the route into the Dead City. The written instructions to kill Zak expose Gort’s handwriting. Confronted with the evidence, the captain turns against the authority he formerly served and declares that he will rule the village himself. He flees to gather the forest men. Erfar urges Zak to stop him before he can return; the ensuing pursuit ends Gort’s rebellion. [[character/nsheriff]] becomes the new captain. Unlike his predecessor, Rivar admits that he dislikes fighting, shares his family’s secret of strength and later supports Zak when suspicion finally reaches the elder.

entries.search: Tka-Rik’s underground dwelling is the turning point between Zak’s local search and his journey across the allods. Here the magician asks him to find surviving Joons, receives his discoveries and finally helps reveal the truth about At-Zako. The Hermit needs the water diverted by the orcs restored. Zak raises their dam and blocks the diversion canal; in return the lizard locates the magician in a ravine in the Remote Mountains. This information joins the tunnel instructions from the Khadaganian report. Zak passes the ancient defences and reaches [[character/rick]]. Tka-Rik explains that his dragonet has watched Zak since his unusual arrival. Bound to Gipath by his duty as its Great Magician, he offers help with Zak’s memory in exchange for bringing him two surviving young Joons. The first journey will be to Ingos to find the girl. Zak must leave his Gipath companions behind. Tka-Rik supplies an amulet for the return journey, but warns that it will work only once the girl has been found; his dragonet will travel with Zak. Tka-Rik places Gipath’s isolation in a longer history. Before the Sundering it belonged to a continent; the Joon civilisation and later states have left successive layers of ruins. The Night of Troubles destroyed many of those later realms. Cania and Khadagan survived, but Tka-Rik distinguishes their societies: he regards Cania as comparatively free, while warning that Khadagan subordinates everyone to someone stronger. His account gives Zak a wider setting for the local ruins and conflicts. The former punishment cell is empty. Zak follows the trail deeper into the Forbidden Catacombs until he finds [[character/deva]], who first mistakes him for another captor. She has escaped the mercenaries and found protection through the ancient treaty between Joons and Wormheads. She rejects the nickname Princess and explains that Diera imprisoned her out of jealousy over the governor. Zak falls in love with her, but she remains faithful to At-Zako, who drew the Joon Curse away from her. Zak promises to respect that bond. They return to Tka-Rik, and the next mission becomes the search for her missing beloved on Suslanger. Before Zak leaves for Suslanger, Tka-Rik describes the Khadaganian hierarchy, in which even a master is subject to someone above him. Emperor Neseb is himself a powerful magician. Suslanger is a provincial backwater, but that does not make it safe. The old Joon portal provides a route there; informants and imperial attention make open enquiries about the missing Joon dangerous. Tka-Rik initially expects Zak to bring the missing Joon with him. Lu-a-Jalla defends the exhausted traveller, and Zak insists that he will continue for her sake even if reunion with At-Zako means losing her. The amulet changes everything: Tka-Rik discovers that its destination was Gipath. Only Zak arrived there in that unusual way. The man he has been seeking is himself, hidden by the Khadaganian transformation spell. Restored as At-Zako, he reassures Tka-Rik and reunites with Lu-a-Jalla. The memories of their earlier flight explain why the return of his identity also brings back the danger of the Curse. If companions have come from Suslanger, Tka-Rik sends them back by a safe route beyond the imperial guards. Their departure does not mean that they have settled on Gipath. The hurried transformation that concealed At-Zako nearly destroyed his memory. Tka-Rik cannot safely repeat it, so hiding as Zak is no longer an answer. He offers another choice: flee again under his temporary protection, or confront the Curse on Gipath. At-Zako chooses to defend his life with Lu-a-Jalla. Tka-Rik supplies ancient Joon equipment and joins him in the catacombs for the final battle. Defeating the Curse completes the campaign.

entries.search: Ingos belongs to Cania. Its thinly populated provinces leave room for independent communities and the Woodsfolk. A governor and city guards represent imperial authority, but the original gazetteer stresses the inhabitants’ independence. Snowy country, mines, forests and older underground ruins surround the city. On [[allod/ingos]], Zak first crosses the hostile countryside to reach the city. [[character/kapitan]] tells him about the missing young woman known locally as the Princess and the reward offered for finding her. Governor [[character/huber]] takes a personal interest in her, while [[character/magess]] discourages the search. The hunter [[character/trapper]] provides a concrete lead: another investigator, the Snoop from the capital, had followed the same trail before disappearing east of the city. Finding his body changes the search for a missing girl into an investigation of murder. The arrow in the Snoop’s body appears to implicate the Woodsfolk. Sver explains that their markings identify a clan, while the governor discovers that the case containing similar arrows has been stolen from his collection. Two lines of inquiry now run alongside each other: the stolen collection and the Woodsfolk’s testimony. To approach [[character/ycf]], Zak first returns the Green Clan’s Sacred Flower after rescuing its keeper from the White Clan. Grey Leaf then asks for help with the kidnapped elder Khabburu and his captor. The clan ultimately identifies the murder arrow as a false attribution, even refusing to blame its enemies for it. When the clan moves, Zak receives access to its hidden route and new home. [[character/shopper]] first lets Baldie’s name slip while boasting that mechanical traps are better than magical ones, then denies knowing anything useful. Tilvar mentions the merchant’s mechanical grinder and the disruption caused when it breaks. Sver knows how to turn these leads into pressure. Zak first delivers the hunter’s furs to a buyer outside the merchant’s monopoly. Sver then reveals Karansul’s hidden trade and unpaid taxes, pointing to the foreman’s accounts; he also recommends [[character/mthief]] as a teacher. With the accounts as leverage, Zak learns where to find [[character/vor]], called Baldie, and secures a meeting. Her urgent warnings against the abandoned mines reinforce his suspicion. Tilvar explains that the governor holds the key. Karansul suggests winning it with a gold nugget and gives access to a dangerous pit, concealing the tigers that drove out its workers; Sver warns Zak of the trap. Zak obtains the nugget and presents it to the collector-governor as a business prospect. Valrasian releases the mine key, opening the way past Diera’s mercenaries. The former punishment cell is empty. Zak follows the trail deeper into the Forbidden Catacombs until he finds [[character/deva]], who first mistakes him for another captor. She has escaped the mercenaries and found protection through the ancient treaty between Joons and Wormheads. She rejects the nickname Princess and explains that Diera imprisoned her out of jealousy over the governor. Zak falls in love with her, but she remains faithful to At-Zako, who drew the Joon Curse away from her. Zak promises to respect that bond. entries.search: [[character/karh]] is the Khadaganian lieutenant who presents the captured Zak to Aiset-Bek. He arranges the prisoner hunt in Death Canyon and threatens punishment even beyond death if Zak fails to entertain his superior. The Odalisque, whom he enslaves, helps Zak escape and points out that Kardaur will be guarding the gate. Zak is captured near the portal on [[allod/suslanger]]. Lieutenant [[character/karh]] presents him to [[character/iz]], who orders him used as live quarry for soldiers seeking promotion. Surviving the run through Death Canyon earns only a return to captivity, not freedom. Kardaur threatens punishment through necromancy if Zak dies too quickly and displeases his superior. The [[character/nalo]] approaches Zak after his ordeal. Enslaved by Kardaur and deprived even of a personal name, she wants his death and knows he will guard the gate that night. She steals the key to Zak’s cage. Her father, a rat hunter who disappeared in the caves, told her of the Wormheads’ temple and the bridges across its lava rivers. She uses that knowledge to explain a route the guards fear to follow. Zak kills Kardaur for the fortress key and escapes toward the cave; releasing the caged spiders can delay pursuit. The Odalisque and Zak part with wishes for each other’s freedom and survival, without a stated account of her later fate.

entries.search: [[character/nekro]] is a disgraced necromancer living in the Last Shelter. Bitter about the Guild’s intrigues, he interprets generosity and honour as disguises for greed and revenge. He asks Zak to destroy a harpy from his experiments and directs the search for At-Zako toward Joon scholars and the rival necromancer Kholai. entries.search: The Khadaganian expedition has established a foothold on Gipath in pursuit of the meteorite. Zak’s capture connects its officers, the Hermit Lizard and the struggle over the island’s secrets. Estera introduces a lost Khadaganian [[character/clerk|official]], who promises that his expedition can help Zak leave Gipath. Meeting [[character/hwleader]] instead leads to imprisonment and demands for information about a meteorite. Zak plays the ignorant swineherd, but the commander threatens torture. [[character/oliz]] offers escape on the condition that Zak later visit his home. Zak gives his word, receives the Ancient Claw for the traps on the approach and escapes. The Hermit explains that he had intended to negotiate with the armoured humans but changed his mind after seeing their treatment of Zak. Keeping the promise establishes trust where the expedition failed to do so.

entries.search: A former warrior under Gort, Khador fell out with his commander and now welcomes the chance to fight beside Zak. His eagerness for battle is more prominent than any grand cause. He stays associated with the village and warns that a crowded party would get in the way of his axe. Khador, usually called Rowdy, served under Gort and was once his friend. After an episode involving mushrooms and an outspoken quarrel, the two stopped speaking. Free of his former duties, Rowdy offers Zak his axe and enthusiasm for a fight. His recruitment is optional, and other business can temporarily keep him in the village. When Zak leaves Gipath alone, Rowdy accepts the farewell and hopes he will return safely.

entries.search: Kharad once hunted people like the fugitives of the Last Shelter. Disillusioned by his Khadaganian superiors, he now seeks revenge and offers his fighting skills to Zak. Loyalty to the brotherhood and his unfinished quarrel with the authorities keep him in Suslanger. Kharad once hunted people like Zak in imperial service. Disillusionment with his superiors turned him against them and brought him to the brotherhood. He offers to make his revenge useful to Zak’s search, while Zak asks him to temper enthusiasm with caution. Khatul’s need for a guard at the Shelter can prevent his recruitment. If he reaches Gipath with Zak, his farewell rejects a new life there: loyalty to the brothers and unfinished revenge call him back to Suslanger.

entries.search: The Last Shelter is a concealed community of fugitives led by Brother Khatul. Its smith, fighters, thieves and disgraced necromancer help Zak investigate Suslanger. Solidarity and fear of discovery shape their decisions, while the Faceless Brother hides a danger within the refuge. Beyond the caves, [[character/kuzn]] finds Zak and vouches for him before [[character/glav]]. The brotherhood’s leader fears imperial spies and requires the Emperor’s Signet Ring, taken from a cyclops who killed its courier. Possessing such an object compromises the newcomer with the authorities and makes the test more than a feat of strength. After Zak returns, Khatul accepts him as Brother Blondie and offers the refuge as a new home. Zak explains his promise to find At-Zako and return to Gipath. Khatul respects that purpose and asks those who can help to support him; [[character/guru]] can teach him greater dexterity. The Shelter’s inhabitants can ask for help with their own grievances alongside the search for At-Zako. Brother Blacksmith wants the slavedriver brothers Lash-Aga and Whip-Aga killed at the plantations. If Zak carries out the request, the workers raise the alarm instead of helping him. The smith explains that imperial law threatens them with death if they fail to report a stranger, then promises to repay the revenge. Kehel offers a separate commission: destroy a harpy he once experimented on, so rivals cannot claim his work. After its death, he admits that fear of Zak’s strength is what makes him honour the promised reward. Their requests expose different consequences of life under the empire: coerced obedience among the workers, personal revenge among its fugitives, and rivalry among its scholars. [[character/merc10]] supplies the next lead through her own theft. Antiquities she stole from [[character/junofil]] remain hidden near the city, and Zak recovers them to arrange a meeting. Khatul and Brother Blacksmith help choose the secluded trading place, keeping strangers away from the Shelter. Baluddin admits recognising At-Zako as a living Joon and wanting to keep him in his own house. Imperial scholars took the young man away. Later, Taivo summoned the collector to identify those scholars’ mutilated bodies. The missing youth’s trail now leads to the necromancers rather than a living prisoner whom Zak can simply rescue. Sahilia can also direct Zak to wealthy properties near the Portal and in the city region. These are optional thefts alongside the search for At-Zako. When offering to accompany him, she says that all her belongings are already with her and that she wants to profit from his good luck. If she travels as far as Gipath, she asks to return: a land without rich houses offers little scope for her talents. [[character/nekro]] directs Zak to [[character/oldnekro]], whom Taivo displaced from the imperial laboratory. Kholai wants disgrace for his rival rather than a simple assassination. Zak steals a dead scientist’s head from the laboratory; its disappearance will embarrass Taivo, and Kholai can summon its spirit. The [[character/spirit|scientist]] describes a horror pursuing the red-skinned youth. To conceal him, the scholars changed his appearance and sent him away by teleportation. Kholai interprets the broken testimony and tells Zak to search the ruined mansion for the magical object used in the escape. The fragments Zak finds are beyond Kehel’s ability to interpret: only a Great Magician can identify the destination. Kholai can also give Zak an experimental object to test in combat. He is interested in the result even if the trial kills its user, a further sign of the limits of his concern for his visitor. Khatul asks [[character/zaku]] to help Zak reach the guarded portal. Faceless arranges a cave meeting and explains the keys and stone controls. He then reveals himself as Erfar: born on Suslanger, he went to Gipath seeking the meteorite and manipulated the villagers into searching for it. His earlier plots were attempts to remove Zak, who disrupted that scheme. The reunion is another trap, with guards waiting outside the cave. Zak survives the confrontation and forces a route through the portal’s defences. Activating its two controls finally returns him to Tka-Rik with the amulet fragments.

entries.search: The Hermit Lizard’s home is a refuge with its own urgent problem: access to water. His bargain with Zak links a rescue, the orcs’ dam and the difficult route toward the Great Magician. Estera introduces a lost Khadaganian [[character/clerk|official]], who promises that his expedition can help Zak leave Gipath. Meeting [[character/hwleader]] instead leads to imprisonment and demands for information about a meteorite. Zak plays the ignorant swineherd, but the commander threatens torture. [[character/oliz]] offers escape on the condition that Zak later visit his home. Zak gives his word, receives the Ancient Claw for the traps on the approach and escapes. The Hermit explains that he had intended to negotiate with the armoured humans but changed his mind after seeing their treatment of Zak. Keeping the promise establishes trust where the expedition failed to do so. The Hermit offers more than directions. He gives Zak an object resembling a horn or shell, hoping it will help him survive, although he cannot explain how a human should use it. His advice about treasure is less benevolent. During their negotiations he points Zak toward the southern lizard islands and says their gold will be his. Zak can follow that lead, only to find hostile owners who pursue the intruder. When confronted, the Hermit calls the misleading invitation a joke, imitating the humour Zak had used with him. Zak makes clear that he does not find the experience amusing. The Hermit needs the water diverted by the orcs restored. Zak raises their dam and blocks the diversion canal; in return the lizard locates the magician in a ravine in the Remote Mountains. This information joins the tunnel instructions from the Khadaganian report. Zak passes the ancient defences and reaches [[character/rick]]. Tka-Rik explains that his dragonet has watched Zak since his unusual arrival. Bound to Gipath by his duty as its Great Magician, he offers help with Zak’s memory in exchange for bringing him two surviving young Joons. The first journey will be to Ingos to find the girl. Zak must leave his Gipath companions behind. Tka-Rik supplies an amulet for the return journey, but warns that it will work only once the girl has been found; his dragonet will travel with Zak.

entries.search: [[character/deva]] is a young Joon and At-Zako’s beloved. On Ingos she is sought as the missing Princess. Diera imprisons her, believing her a rival for the governor’s affection, although Lu-a-Jalla says she loves only At-Zako. Zak brings her to Tka Rik and continues searching for her lover. Their reunion comes when Zak’s true identity is revealed, but the Joon Curse still threatens their future. The former punishment cell is empty. Zak follows the trail deeper into the Forbidden Catacombs until he finds [[character/deva]], who first mistakes him for another captor. She has escaped the mercenaries and found protection through the ancient treaty between Joons and Wormheads. She rejects the nickname Princess and explains that Diera imprisoned her out of jealousy over the governor. Zak falls in love with her, but she remains faithful to At-Zako, who drew the Joon Curse away from her. Zak promises to respect that bond. They return to Tka-Rik, and the next mission becomes the search for her missing beloved on Suslanger. Tka-Rik initially expects Zak to bring the missing Joon with him. Lu-a-Jalla defends the exhausted traveller, and Zak insists that he will continue for her sake even if reunion with At-Zako means losing her. The amulet changes everything: Tka-Rik discovers that its destination was Gipath. Only Zak arrived there in that unusual way. The man he has been seeking is himself, hidden by the Khadaganian transformation spell. Restored as At-Zako, he reassures Tka-Rik and reunites with Lu-a-Jalla. The memories of their earlier flight explain why the return of his identity also brings back the danger of the Curse. If companions have come from Suslanger, Tka-Rik sends them back by a safe route beyond the imperial guards. Their departure does not mean that they have settled on Gipath. The hurried transformation that concealed At-Zako nearly destroyed his memory. Tka-Rik cannot safely repeat it, so hiding as Zak is no longer an answer. He offers another choice: flee again under his temporary protection, or confront the Curse on Gipath. At-Zako chooses to defend his life with Lu-a-Jalla. Tka-Rik supplies ancient Joon equipment and joins him in the catacombs for the final battle. Defeating the Curse completes the campaign.

entries.search: Mairana is an Ingos archer who offers Zak protection outside the city walls. She seeks the experience needed to enter the Mercenaries’ Guild rather than immediate pay. Ingos remains her home, and she declines to leave it when Zak’s search moves on. Mairana introduces herself as an archer useful outside the city walls, where the population is hostile to strangers. She cannot yet demand a mercenary’s fee because she has not joined the Guild: experience is her immediate reward. A required permit can delay her departure from the city. While waiting, she avoids provoking Tilvar’s suspicions and credits Zak with improving the guards’ attitude towards her. At the end of their association, she explicitly chooses to remain on Ingos, which she considers her home.

entries.search: The river islands hold two different leads. Estera needs the Orb, which Erfar places on the southernmost island. Erfar also proposes tracing [[character/bgoblinc]]’s blue Eye Stone to a possible portal. Zak takes the First Goblin’s skull to compel GoGo to visit the village; the chief explains that the orcs confiscated the written record of the stone’s origin. The islands require their own bridge mechanism, distinct from the cave’s. Zak retrieves the record and the Orb in this area. Erfar claims the record offers nothing useful, then diverts attention to missing taxes and gold in Golden Valley. His portal scheme and Estera’s search serve different purposes, even though they take Zak through the same territory. Airy returns with a lead to the old observatory library, but harpies occupy the site. Her plan requires a lizard’s amulet to lead a particular green dragon against them. Reaching that dragon requires Estera to freeze the lake with a green crystal. The hostile lizards on the approach present another obstacle: Zak moves the Big Shell from the Remote Mountains to the Middle Mountains, restoring the peace associated with its altar. This leaves Babur’s former quarry route unsafe and can lead to an additional errand for the craftsman. The observatory book finally supplies the password to the Dead City’s hidden entrance. Airy can also teach Zak the Magic of Feelings, only to be offended when he again calls her a little girl. After Gort’s fall, Erfar claims that an orc seer has cursed the village with disease and asks for a White Flower. Babur wants to monopolise the healing flower and charge Erfar ruinous prices; Zak rebukes him. Zak finds armed opposition waiting for him, although no villagers have yet fallen ill. Erfar blames Babur, while Babur’s earlier warning makes Zak suspect both men. Estera suggests setting a trap. Zak tells each suspect a different location for a second flower; the ambush appears at the place he gave Erfar. With Rivar’s support he confronts and imprisons the elder. An expedition report recovered from the abandoned foreign camp becomes leverage: Erfar translates its account of a concealed tunnel and its opening lever. He later escapes custody. Estera recalls that he originally arrived as an adult stranger, leaving his real purpose unresolved. Babur welcomes the exposure and says that the villagers feared Erfar rather than loved him. Before leaving Gipath, Zak can finish the separate search for Airy, who set out to find the magician herself and impress him. Estera’s vision points to a goblin prison, where Zak finds her granddaughter’s potion bottle and a note leading to [[character/orcc]]. The orc chief intends to give Airy to a frightening armoured human he calls a Demon. Zak offers to remove this threat instead. Shei-Var first demands proof of his strength against the ogre brothers, whose wealth also threatens the chief’s influence. Once Zak defeats the Demon, Shei-Var honours his promise and sends Airy home. The rescue ends with Estera’s gratitude and Airy’s distress that Zak still regards her as a child.

entries.search: Naya is Estera’s apprentice and has long hunted on her teacher’s behalf. Estera offers her help to Zak as a test of her training. Naya wants her abilities respected and hopes one day to succeed Estera and teach an apprentice of her own. Estera introduces Naya as her apprentice and offers her assistance as a test of her training. Naya corrects the impression that she lacks experience: she already hunts for the witch and has faced goblins and orcs. If recruited, she travels as a capable assistant rather than an untrained dependent. At parting she hopes to succeed Estera and teach an apprentice of her own. Her cryptic farewell hints at a change awaiting Zak, but she refuses to explain what she sees.

entries.search: Beyond the caves, [[character/kuzn]] finds Zak and vouches for him before [[character/glav]]. The brotherhood’s leader fears imperial spies and requires the Emperor’s Signet Ring, taken from a cyclops who killed its courier. Possessing such an object compromises the newcomer with the authorities and makes the test more than a feat of strength. After Zak returns, Khatul accepts him as Brother Blondie and offers the refuge as a new home. Zak explains his promise to find At-Zako and return to Gipath. Khatul respects that purpose and asks those who can help to support him; [[character/guru]] can teach him greater dexterity. The Shelter’s inhabitants can ask for help with their own grievances alongside the search for At-Zako. Brother Blacksmith wants the slavedriver brothers Lash-Aga and Whip-Aga killed at the plantations. If Zak carries out the request, the workers raise the alarm instead of helping him. The smith explains that imperial law threatens them with death if they fail to report a stranger, then promises to repay the revenge. Kehel offers a separate commission: destroy a harpy he once experimented on, so rivals cannot claim his work. After its death, he admits that fear of Zak’s strength is what makes him honour the promised reward. Their requests expose different consequences of life under the empire: coerced obedience among the workers, personal revenge among its fugitives, and rivalry among its scholars. [[character/nekro]] directs Zak to [[character/oldnekro]], whom Taivo displaced from the imperial laboratory. Kholai wants disgrace for his rival rather than a simple assassination. Zak steals a dead scientist’s head from the laboratory; its disappearance will embarrass Taivo, and Kholai can summon its spirit. The [[character/spirit|scientist]] describes a horror pursuing the red-skinned youth. To conceal him, the scholars changed his appearance and sent him away by teleportation. Kholai interprets the broken testimony and tells Zak to search the ruined mansion for the magical object used in the escape. The fragments Zak finds are beyond Kehel’s ability to interpret: only a Great Magician can identify the destination. Kholai can also give Zak an experimental object to test in combat. He is interested in the result even if the trial kills its user, a further sign of the limits of his concern for his visitor.

entries.search: The Green Clan’s new residence reflects its displacement during the Ingos story. It continues to connect Zak with the Woodsfolk and Brissen, whose ideal of service to good exists beside the clan’s harsher methods. The arrow in the Snoop’s body appears to implicate the Woodsfolk. Sver explains that their markings identify a clan, while the governor discovers that the case containing similar arrows has been stolen from his collection. Two lines of inquiry now run alongside each other: the stolen collection and the Woodsfolk’s testimony. To approach [[character/ycf]], Zak first returns the Green Clan’s Sacred Flower after rescuing its keeper from the White Clan. Grey Leaf then asks for help with the kidnapped elder Khabburu and his captor. The clan ultimately identifies the murder arrow as a false attribution, even refusing to blame its enemies for it. When the clan moves, Zak receives access to its hidden route and new home. At the Green Clan’s new home, Grey Leaf describes the supposed man in grey as a white-haired woman. Zak identifies Diera, whose own traps protected the stolen collection. Her urgent warnings against the abandoned mines reinforce his suspicion. Tilvar explains that the governor holds the key. Karansul suggests winning it with a gold nugget and gives access to a dangerous pit, concealing the tigers that drove out its workers; Sver warns Zak of the trap. Zak obtains the nugget and presents it to the collector-governor as a business prospect. Valrasian releases the mine key, opening the way past Diera’s mercenaries.

She uses that knowledge to explain a route the guards fear to follow. Zak kills Kardaur for the fortress key and escapes toward the cave; releasing the caged spiders can delay pursuit. The Odalisque and Zak part with wishes for each other’s freedom and survival, without a stated account of her later fate.

entries.search: [[character/skd]] inhabits the mountain lair where Zak expects to find a magician. Amused by the visitor, he invokes old traditions and offers answers in return for a task: poison the underground spring used by the noisy armadillos beneath his home. The meeting turns a mistaken destination into another lead in Zak’s search. The observatory’s password takes Zak into the Dead City and up Lone Mountain. He expects the magician from the Orb but finds [[character/skd]]. The dragon insists on an old bargain: a visitor must perform a task before receiving an answer. Zak deals with the armadillos beneath the lair, using the poison the dragon supplies. The dragon then admits that he cannot identify Zak or locate Gipath’s elusive Great Magician. He suggests the ancient lizards might know more and points instead to an expedition of armoured outsiders. He withdraws the skeletons he had used against their camp. In a further conversation, he gives Zak an old sword because he enjoys his company and would rather not see him become another speechless skeleton.

entries.search: Sahilia can also direct Zak to wealthy properties near the Portal and in the city region. These are optional thefts alongside the search for At-Zako. When offering to accompany him, she says that all her belongings are already with her and that she wants to profit from his good luck. If she travels as far as Gipath, she asks to return: a land without rich houses offers little scope for her talents. Khatul asks [[character/zaku]] to help Zak reach the guarded portal. Faceless arranges a cave meeting and explains the keys and stone controls. He then reveals himself as Erfar: born on Suslanger, he went to Gipath seeking the meteorite and manipulated the villagers into searching for it. His earlier plots were attempts to remove Zak, who disrupted that scheme. The reunion is another trap, with guards waiting outside the cave. Zak survives the confrontation and forces a route through the portal’s defences. Activating its two controls finally returns him to Tka-Rik with the amulet fragments.

entries.search: [[character/nsheriff]] becomes captain after Gort. Though exceptionally strong, he admits that he dislikes fighting and is no gifted speaker. He shares his family’s secret of strength with Zak and supports him against Erfar. His later admission that the prisoner escaped shows the limits of his vigilance. entries.search: Sahilia is a thief living in the Last Shelter. Her stolen Joon antiquities give Zak a lead to the collector Baluddin, while her knowledge of hiding places and wealthy houses opens other opportunities. She can accompany him, but asks to return to Suslanger rather than stay on Gipath, where she would have few profitable targets. [[character/merc10]] supplies the next lead through her own theft. Khatul and Brother Blacksmith help choose the secluded trading place, keeping strangers away from the Shelter. Baluddin admits recognising At-Zako as a living Joon and wanting to keep him in his own house. Imperial scholars took the young man away. Later, Taivo summoned the collector to identify those scholars’ mutilated bodies. The missing youth’s trail now leads to the necromancers rather than a living prisoner whom Zak can simply rescue. When offering to accompany him, she says that all her belongings are already with her and that she wants to profit from his good luck. The promised friendly meeting becomes an ambush by brigands and village soldiers. Erfar denies responsibility. Gort blames drunken, undisciplined soldiers and brigands dressed as villagers, then briefly threatens to overthrow Erfar before withdrawing the threat. Babur warns that the elder is trying to have Zak killed. A note in the newer orc script cannot yet settle the matter: Estera needs an Orc ABC Book to read it. Its translation reveals a contract on Zak’s life, a detailed description of him and a substantial payment. The search for the author becomes a separate investigation alongside the route into the Dead City. Estera introduces a lost Khadaganian [[character/clerk|official]], who promises that his expedition can help Zak leave Gipath. [[character/oliz]] offers escape on the condition that Zak later visit his home. Zak gives his word, receives the Ancient Claw for the traps on the approach and escapes. entries.search: Suslanger is a dry Khadaganian allod with little cultivable land. A river, lake, dams and irrigation channels sustain its settlements. The old Joon portal provides a route there; informants and imperial attention make open enquiries about the missing Joon dangerous. Zak is captured near the portal on [[allod/suslanger]]. Lieutenant [[character/karh]] presents him to [[character/iz]], who orders him used as live quarry for soldiers seeking promotion. The [[character/nalo]] approaches Zak after his ordeal. Enslaved by Kardaur and deprived even of a personal name, she wants his death and knows he will guard the gate that night. She steals the key to Zak’s cage. Her father, a rat hunter who disappeared in the caves, told her of the Wormheads’ temple and the bridges across its lava rivers. She uses that knowledge to explain a route the guards fear to follow. Zak kills Kardaur for the fortress key and escapes toward the cave; releasing the caged spiders can delay pursuit. The Odalisque and Zak part with wishes for each other’s freedom and survival, without a stated account of her later fate. Khatul respects that purpose and asks those who can help to support him; [[character/guru]] can teach him greater dexterity. The Shelter’s inhabitants can ask for help with their own grievances alongside the search for At-Zako. Brother Blacksmith wants the slavedriver brothers Lash-Aga and Whip-Aga killed at the plantations. If Zak carries out the request, the workers raise the alarm instead of helping him. The smith explains that imperial law threatens them with death if they fail to report a stranger, then promises to repay the revenge. Kehel offers a separate commission: destroy a harpy he once experimented on, so rivals cannot claim his work. After its death, he admits that fear of Zak’s strength is what makes him honour the promised reward. Their requests expose different consequences of life under the empire: coerced obedience among the workers, personal revenge among its fugitives, and rivalry among its scholars. Khatul and Brother Blacksmith help choose the secluded trading place, keeping strangers away from the Shelter. Later, Taivo summoned the collector to identify those scholars’ mutilated bodies. The missing youth’s trail now leads to the necromancers rather than a living prisoner whom Zak can simply rescue. Faceless arranges a cave meeting and explains the keys and stone controls. He then reveals himself as Erfar: born on Suslanger, he went to Gipath seeking the meteorite and manipulated the villagers into searching for it. His earlier plots were attempts to remove Zak, who disrupted that scheme. The reunion is another trap, with guards waiting outside the cave. entries.search: [[character/trapper]] is an experienced Ingos hunter who knows the Woodsfolk and their customs. He helps Zak investigate the murdered Snoop and explains how to gain the Green Clan’s trust. He also resents Karansul’s control over the fur trade. In return for help selling his skins, Sver reveals the merchant’s concealed accounts and recommends the thief [[character/mthief]]. On [[allod/ingos]], Zak first crosses the hostile countryside to reach the city. [[character/kapitan]] tells him about the missing young woman known locally as the Princess and the reward offered for finding her. Governor [[character/huber]] takes a personal interest in her, while [[character/magess]] discourages the search. The hunter [[character/trapper]] provides a concrete lead: another investigator, the Snoop from the capital, had followed the same trail before disappearing east of the city. Finding his body changes the search for a missing girl into an investigation of murder. The arrow in the Snoop’s body appears to implicate the Woodsfolk. Sver explains that their markings identify a clan, while the governor discovers that the case containing similar arrows has been stolen from his collection. Two lines of inquiry now run alongside each other: the stolen collection and the Woodsfolk’s testimony. To approach [[character/ycf]], Zak first returns the Green Clan’s Sacred Flower after rescuing its keeper from the White Clan. Grey Leaf then asks for help with the kidnapped elder Khabburu and his captor. The clan ultimately identifies the murder arrow as a false attribution, even refusing to blame its enemies for it. When the clan moves, Zak receives access to its hidden route and new home. [[character/shopper]] first lets Baldie’s name slip while boasting that mechanical traps are better than magical ones, then denies knowing anything useful. Tilvar mentions the merchant’s mechanical grinder and the disruption caused when it breaks. Sver knows how to turn these leads into pressure. Zak first delivers the hunter’s furs to a buyer outside the merchant’s monopoly. Sver then reveals Karansul’s hidden trade and unpaid taxes, pointing to the foreman’s accounts; he also recommends [[character/mthief]] as a teacher. With the accounts as leverage, Zak learns where to find [[character/vor]], called Baldie, and secures a meeting. Evidence from the stolen collection makes the thief confess: he killed the Snoop, planted the Woodsfolk arrow and worked for a cloaked employer who knew how to evade the governor’s magical traps. At the Green Clan’s new home, Grey Leaf describes the supposed man in grey as a white-haired woman. Zak identifies Diera, whose own traps protected the stolen collection. Her urgent warnings against the abandoned mines reinforce his suspicion. Tilvar explains that the governor holds the key. Karansul suggests winning it with a gold nugget and gives access to a dangerous pit, concealing the tigers that drove out its workers; Sver warns Zak of the trap. Zak obtains the nugget and presents it to the collector-governor as a business prospect. Valrasian releases the mine key, opening the way past Diera’s mercenaries.

entries.search: The Shelter’s inhabitants can ask for help with their own grievances alongside the search for At-Zako. Brother Blacksmith wants the slavedriver brothers Lash-Aga and Whip-Aga killed at the plantations. If Zak carries out the request, the workers raise the alarm instead of helping him. The smith explains that imperial law threatens them with death if they fail to report a stranger, then promises to repay the revenge. Kehel offers a separate commission: destroy a harpy he once experimented on, so rivals cannot claim his work. After its death, he admits that fear of Zak’s strength is what makes him honour the promised reward. Their requests expose different consequences of life under the empire: coerced obedience among the workers, personal revenge among its fugitives, and rivalry among its scholars. [[character/merc10]] supplies the next lead through her own theft. Antiquities she stole from [[character/junofil]] remain hidden near the city, and Zak recovers them to arrange a meeting. Khatul and Brother Blacksmith help choose the secluded trading place, keeping strangers away from the Shelter. Baluddin admits recognising At-Zako as a living Joon and wanting to keep him in his own house. Imperial scholars took the young man away. Later, Taivo summoned the collector to identify those scholars’ mutilated bodies. The missing youth’s trail now leads to the necromancers rather than a living prisoner whom Zak can simply rescue. Sahilia can also direct Zak to wealthy properties near the Portal and in the city region. These are optional thefts alongside the search for At-Zako. When offering to accompany him, she says that all her belongings are already with her and that she wants to profit from his good luck. If she travels as far as Gipath, she asks to return: a land without rich houses offers little scope for her talents. [[character/nekro]] directs Zak to [[character/oldnekro]], whom Taivo displaced from the imperial laboratory. Kholai wants disgrace for his rival rather than a simple assassination. Zak steals a dead scientist’s head from the laboratory; its disappearance will embarrass Taivo, and Kholai can summon its spirit. The [[character/spirit|scientist]] describes a horror pursuing the red-skinned youth. To conceal him, the scholars changed his appearance and sent him away by teleportation. Kholai interprets the broken testimony and tells Zak to search the ruined mansion for the magical object used in the escape. The fragments Zak finds are beyond Kehel’s ability to interpret: only a Great Magician can identify the destination. Kholai can also give Zak an experimental object to test in combat. He is interested in the result even if the trial kills its user, a further sign of the limits of his concern for his visitor.

entries.search: [[character/kapitan]] commands the guards in the governor’s city on Ingos. He serves Valrasian’s interests and discourages Zak from pursuing the missing Princess. The arrow found in a murdered investigator gives him a pretext for action against the Woodsfolk. His later advice about the sealed mines is useful, but he openly resents an outsider who might outshine his officers. On [[allod/ingos]], Zak first crosses the hostile countryside to reach the city. [[character/kapitan]] tells him about the missing young woman known locally as the Princess and the reward offered for finding her. Governor [[character/huber]] takes a personal interest in her, while [[character/magess]] discourages the search. The hunter [[character/trapper]] provides a concrete lead: another investigator, the Snoop from the capital, had followed the same trail before disappearing east of the city. Finding his body changes the search for a missing girl into an investigation of murder. The arrow in the Snoop’s body appears to implicate the Woodsfolk. Sver explains that their markings identify a clan, while the governor discovers that the case containing similar arrows has been stolen from his collection. Two lines of inquiry now run alongside each other: the stolen collection and the Woodsfolk’s testimony. To approach [[character/ycf]], Zak first returns the Green Clan’s Sacred Flower after rescuing its keeper from the White Clan. Grey Leaf then asks for help with the kidnapped elder Khabburu and his captor. The clan ultimately identifies the murder arrow as a false attribution, even refusing to blame its enemies for it. When the clan moves, Zak receives access to its hidden route and new home. [[character/shopper]] first lets Baldie’s name slip while boasting that mechanical traps are better than magical ones, then denies knowing anything useful. Tilvar mentions the merchant’s mechanical grinder and the disruption caused when it breaks. Sver knows how to turn these leads into pressure. Zak first delivers the hunter’s furs to a buyer outside the merchant’s monopoly. Sver then reveals Karansul’s hidden trade and unpaid taxes, pointing to the foreman’s accounts; he also recommends [[character/mthief]] as a teacher. With the accounts as leverage, Zak learns where to find [[character/vor]], called Baldie, and secures a meeting. Evidence from the stolen collection makes the thief confess: he killed the Snoop, planted the Woodsfolk arrow and worked for a cloaked employer who knew how to evade the governor’s magical traps. At the Green Clan’s new home, Grey Leaf describes the supposed man in grey as a white-haired woman. Zak identifies Diera, whose own traps protected the stolen collection. Her urgent warnings against the abandoned mines reinforce his suspicion. Tilvar explains that the governor holds the key. Karansul suggests winning it with a gold nugget and gives access to a dangerous pit, concealing the tigers that drove out its workers; Sver warns Zak of the trap. Zak obtains the nugget and presents it to the collector-governor as a business prospect. Valrasian releases the mine key, opening the way past Diera’s mercenaries.

entries.search: [[character/rick]] is the Great Magician of Gipath and a survivor of the Joon people. His dragonet watches Zak’s journey before they meet. He explains that a Great Magician cannot leave his island, so he needs Zak to find two young Joons abroad. In return, he offers help with Zak’s lost identity. The Hermit needs the water diverted by the orcs restored. Zak raises their dam and blocks the diversion canal; in return the lizard locates the magician in a ravine in the Remote Mountains. This information joins the tunnel instructions from the Khadaganian report. Zak passes the ancient defences and reaches [[character/rick]]. Tka-Rik explains that his dragonet has watched Zak since his unusual arrival. Bound to Gipath by his duty as its Great Magician, he offers help with Zak’s memory in exchange for bringing him two surviving young Joons. The first journey will be to Ingos to find the girl. Zak must leave his Gipath companions behind. Tka-Rik supplies an amulet for the return journey, but warns that it will work only once the girl has been found; his dragonet will travel with Zak. Tka-Rik places Gipath’s isolation in a longer history. Before the Sundering it belonged to a continent; the Joon civilisation and later states have left successive layers of ruins. The Night of Troubles destroyed many of those later realms. Cania and Khadagan survived, but Tka-Rik distinguishes their societies: he regards Cania as comparatively free, while warning that Khadagan subordinates everyone to someone stronger. His account gives Zak a wider setting for the local ruins and conflicts. The former punishment cell is empty. Zak follows the trail deeper into the Forbidden Catacombs until he finds [[character/deva]], who first mistakes him for another captor. She has escaped the mercenaries and found protection through the ancient treaty between Joons and Wormheads. She rejects the nickname Princess and explains that Diera imprisoned her out of jealousy over the governor. Zak falls in love with her, but she remains faithful to At-Zako, who drew the Joon Curse away from her. Zak promises to respect that bond. They return to Tka-Rik, and the next mission becomes the search for her missing beloved on Suslanger. Before Zak leaves for Suslanger, Tka-Rik describes the Khadaganian hierarchy, in which even a master is subject to someone above him. Emperor Neseb is himself a powerful magician. Suslanger is a provincial backwater, but that does not make it safe. The old Joon portal provides a route there; informants and imperial attention make open enquiries about the missing Joon dangerous. Tka-Rik initially expects Zak to bring the missing Joon with him. Lu-a-Jalla defends the exhausted traveller, and Zak insists that he will continue for her sake even if reunion with At-Zako means losing her. The amulet changes everything: Tka-Rik discovers that its destination was Gipath. Only Zak arrived there in that unusual way. The man he has been seeking is himself, hidden by the Khadaganian transformation spell. Restored as At-Zako, he reassures Tka-Rik and reunites with Lu-a-Jalla. The memories of their earlier flight explain why the return of his identity also brings back the danger of the Curse. If companions have come from Suslanger, Tka-Rik sends them back by a safe route beyond the imperial guards. Their departure does not mean that they have settled on Gipath. The hurried transformation that concealed At-Zako nearly destroyed his memory. Tka-Rik cannot safely repeat it, so hiding as Zak is no longer an answer. He offers another choice: flee again under his temporary protection, or confront the Curse on Gipath. At-Zako chooses to defend his life with Lu-a-Jalla. Tka-Rik supplies ancient Joon equipment and joins him in the catacombs for the final battle. Defeating the Curse completes the campaign.

entries.search: The village is Gipath’s only human settlement. Here Erfar names Zak the Chosen, Gort commands the guards and Babur offers his craft. entries.search: Estera’s secluded cave is a place of advice, bargaining and magical instruction. The witch helps Zak investigate his missing memory, while Airy and Naya connect the cave with the wider life of the village. Before Estera’s formal introduction, Zak can meet Airy at the cave; she warns him about her grandmother and the traps protecting their home. [[character/witch]] initially threatens the intruder, then changes her reception when Zak offers the Magic Bit. She dismisses the villagers’ divine-saviour story but discovers that she cannot see his past. Since Zak cannot remember it either, she suggests finding the orcs’ Magic Orb and directs him back to Erfar for information. This is the beginning of their alliance. Estera also introduces her granddaughter [[character/daughter]], warning Zak to keep his distance; Airy resents being treated as a child. Zak’s search now has a personal aim beyond the village’s demands. When Estera uses the Orb, Zak sees an old man instead of a recognisable memory. She believes he is its owner and a more powerful magician who might help. Orc records trace the object to the Dead City. Estera distinguishes its human fortress from Gipath’s much older ruins: after the Night of Troubles, the dead attacked the living, and survivors fled to found the present village. The obvious route into the fortress is deadly. Airy leaves to investigate another way in, despite her grandmother’s objections. Separately, Erfar can send Zak into the surrounding region’s Golden Valley for a caravan’s lost treasure, an errand he badly understates. Airy returns with a lead to the old observatory library, but harpies occupy the site. Her plan requires a lizard’s amulet to lead a particular green dragon against them. Reaching that dragon requires Estera to freeze the lake with a green crystal. The hostile lizards on the approach present another obstacle: Zak moves the Big Shell from the Remote Mountains to the Middle Mountains, restoring the peace associated with its altar. This leaves Babur’s former quarry route unsafe and can lead to an additional errand for the craftsman. The observatory book finally supplies the password to the Dead City’s hidden entrance. Airy can also teach Zak the Magic of Feelings, only to be offended when he again calls her a little girl. Estera introduces a lost Khadaganian [[character/clerk|official]], who promises that his expedition can help Zak leave Gipath. Meeting [[character/hwleader]] instead leads to imprisonment and demands for information about a meteorite. Zak plays the ignorant swineherd, but the commander threatens torture. [[character/oliz]] offers escape on the condition that Zak later visit his home. Zak gives his word, receives the Ancient Claw for the traps on the approach and escapes. The Hermit explains that he had intended to negotiate with the armoured humans but changed his mind after seeing their treatment of Zak. Keeping the promise establishes trust where the expedition failed to do so. Before leaving Gipath, Zak can finish the separate search for Airy, who set out to find the magician herself and impress him. Estera’s vision points to a goblin prison, where Zak finds her granddaughter’s potion bottle and a note leading to [[character/orcc]]. The orc chief intends to give Airy to a frightening armoured human he calls a Demon. Zak offers to remove this threat instead. Shei-Var first demands proof of his strength against the ogre brothers, whose wealth also threatens the chief’s influence. Once Zak defeats the Demon, Shei-Var honours his promise and sends Airy home. The rescue ends with Estera’s gratitude and Airy’s distress that Zak still regards her as a child.

entries.search: The [[character/nalo]] approaches Zak after his ordeal. Enslaved by Kardaur and deprived even of a personal name, she wants his death and knows he will guard the gate that night. She steals the key to Zak’s cage. Her father, a rat hunter who disappeared in the caves, told her of the Wormheads’ temple and the bridges across its lava rivers. She uses that knowledge to explain a route the guards fear to follow. Zak kills Kardaur for the fortress key and escapes toward the cave; releasing the caged spiders can delay pursuit. The Odalisque and Zak part with wishes for each other’s freedom and survival, without a stated account of her later fate. Beyond the caves, [[character/kuzn]] finds Zak and vouches for him before [[character/glav]]. The brotherhood’s leader fears imperial spies and requires the Emperor’s Signet Ring, taken from a cyclops who killed its courier. Possessing such an object compromises the newcomer with the authorities and makes the test more than a feat of strength. After Zak returns, Khatul accepts him as Brother Blondie and offers the refuge as a new home. Zak explains his promise to find At-Zako and return to Gipath. Khatul respects that purpose and asks those who can help to support him; [[character/guru]] can teach him greater dexterity.
