Leaving the ruins, he sees villagers flee from the stranger who has emerged from the ancient site. Their flight gives him a direction to follow. He makes his way along the river and across the ford to the village. At the village assembly, [[character/elder]] identifies Zak with the promised Chosen who was to appear at the Sacred Ruins. [[character/sheriff]], the captain, supports the ceremony. The offer of food, shelter and honour comes with a threat: an impostor would be thrown into the fire. Zak accepts the title and gives his name. Erfar immediately sends him against the goblin sentry watching the village, reasoning that his plain clothes and unusual metal knife will let him approach where armed villagers cannot. Afterwards Zak learns that this is Gipath’s only human village, with no king or known route to other lands. Killing the sentry brings another request from Erfar: the White Wolf and its pack are taking the village livestock. After Zak kills their leader, Erfar and Gort press him to surrender the head so the captain can claim prestige. Gort also sends him to punish the goblins while the village soldiers stay home. Meanwhile [[character/smith]] refuses to work until his stolen iron tools are returned. Erfar calls the thieves friendly “Free Hunters”; Babur calls them brigands and describes the beating of his apprentice. Recovering the chisel and bodkin from the chief and his wife wins Zak the craftsman’s services. These early errands expose the disagreement between the village’s leaders and the man who equips it. Babur’s account of a red-haired brigand meeting orcs gives Zak his next lead. A map taken from Redhead points to a Magic Bit in a sarcophagus in the orc cave. Babur explains that Estera values such objects, while Gort can supply the missing drawbridge mechanism. Zak obtains the seer’s key and the object, then asks how to reach the witch. Babur, who made her spare trap key, explains the guarded ravines and controlling obelisks. The craftsman expects a share of the sale. Zak instead intends to exchange the find for help with his lost memory. Babur also offers a separate reward for weakening the orcs in the Foothills. Their seer controls an ancient pyramid that strikes intruders with lightning. If Zak accepts, he kills the seer and shuts the device down, allowing the craftsman to travel more safely. When Babur pays him, Zak asks why a land without a king uses royal coins. Babur explains that the money survives from an earlier civilisation. Accessible ruins have already been stripped; richer finds lie in places dangerous enough to discourage even him. Before Estera’s formal introduction, Zak can meet Airy at the cave; she warns him about her grandmother and the traps protecting their home. [[character/witch]] initially threatens the intruder, then changes her reception when Zak offers the Magic Bit. She dismisses the villagers’ divine-saviour story but discovers that she cannot see his past. Since Zak cannot remember it either, she suggests finding the orcs’ Magic Orb and directs him back to Erfar for information. This is the beginning of their alliance. Estera also introduces her granddaughter [[character/daughter]], warning Zak to keep his distance; Airy resents being treated as a child. Zak’s search now has a personal aim beyond the village’s demands. The river islands hold two different leads. Estera needs the Orb, which Erfar places on the southernmost island. Erfar also proposes tracing [[character/bgoblinc]]’s blue Eye Stone to a possible portal. Zak takes the First Goblin’s skull to compel GoGo to visit the village; the chief explains that the orcs confiscated the written record of the stone’s origin. The islands require their own bridge mechanism, distinct from the cave’s. Zak retrieves the record and the Orb in this area. Erfar claims the record offers nothing useful, then diverts attention to missing taxes and gold in Golden Valley. His portal scheme and Estera’s search serve different purposes, even though they take Zak through the same territory. When Estera uses the Orb, Zak sees an old man instead of a recognisable memory. She believes he is its owner and a more powerful magician who might help. Orc records trace the object to the Dead City. Estera distinguishes its human fortress from Gipath’s much older ruins: after the Night of Troubles, the dead attacked the living, and survivors fled to found the present village. The obvious route into the fortress is deadly. Airy leaves to investigate another way in, despite her grandmother’s objections. Separately, Erfar can send Zak into the surrounding region’s Golden Valley for a caravan’s lost treasure, an errand he badly understates. Erfar links the missing village taxes to the disappearance of Babur’s apprentice and accuses the craftsman of plotting to take power. Babur denies the charge: he suspects the brigands of stealing the gold and kidnapping his worker. Erfar proposes replacing the money with treasure from a ruined caravan in Golden Valley. Babur exposes the danger omitted from this offer: earlier visitors vanished, and one survivor returned deranged, speaking of undead guards. Zak can refuse the expedition. Erfar then reproaches him and later claims another man supplied the gold. If Zak instead retrieves it, the elder thanks him with promises of a song and admits that he understated the danger. Neither exchange establishes what actually happened to the apprentice. While Zak seeks the magician, Erfar and Gort arrange another joint operation with the Free Hunters, supposedly to prevent a goblin raid. The promised friendly meeting becomes an ambush by brigands and village soldiers. Erfar denies responsibility. Gort blames drunken, undisciplined soldiers and brigands dressed as villagers, then briefly threatens to overthrow Erfar before withdrawing the threat. Babur warns that the elder is trying to have Zak killed. A note in the newer orc script cannot yet settle the matter: Estera needs an Orc ABC Book to read it. Its translation reveals a contract on Zak’s life, a detailed description of him and a substantial payment. The search for the author becomes a separate investigation alongside the route into the Dead City. Airy returns with a lead to the old observatory library, but harpies occupy the site. Her plan requires a lizard’s amulet to lead a particular green dragon against them. Reaching that dragon requires Estera to freeze the lake with a green crystal. The hostile lizards on the approach present another obstacle: Zak moves the Big Shell from the Remote Mountains to the Middle Mountains, restoring the peace associated with its altar. This leaves Babur’s former quarry route unsafe and can lead to an additional errand for the craftsman. The observatory book finally supplies the password to the Dead City’s hidden entrance. Airy can also teach Zak the Magic of Feelings, only to be offended when he again calls her a little girl. Moving the Big Shell solves one problem and creates another. Babur can no longer use the road protected by its old altar. The alternative route passes a cyclops tending pigs stolen from the village, and the craftsman offers payment to make it safe. Zak can kill the cyclops or destroy its food supply and wait for it to leave. The latter plan depends on remaining unnoticed. Babur pays once access is restored. The dispute shows why his advice about the Shell serves his own livelihood as well as Zak’s journey. The written instructions to kill Zak expose Gort’s handwriting. Confronted with the evidence, the captain turns against the authority he formerly served and declares that he will rule the village himself. He flees to gather the forest men. Erfar urges Zak to stop him before he can return; the ensuing pursuit ends Gort’s rebellion. [[character/nsheriff]] becomes the new captain. Unlike his predecessor, Rivar admits that he dislikes fighting, shares his family’s secret of strength and later supports Zak when suspicion finally reaches the elder. The observatory’s password takes Zak into the Dead City and up Lone Mountain. He expects the magician from the Orb but finds [[character/skd]]. The dragon insists on an old bargain: a visitor must perform a task before receiving an answer. Zak deals with the armadillos beneath the lair, using the poison the dragon supplies. The dragon then admits that he cannot identify Zak or locate Gipath’s elusive Great Magician. He suggests the ancient lizards might know more and points instead to an expedition of armoured outsiders. He withdraws the skeletons he had used against their camp. In a further conversation, he gives Zak an old sword because he enjoys his company and would rather not see him become another speechless skeleton. After Gort’s fall, Erfar claims that an orc seer has cursed the village with disease and asks for a White Flower. Babur wants to monopolise the healing flower and charge Erfar ruinous prices; Zak rebukes him. Zak finds armed opposition waiting for him, although no villagers have yet fallen ill. Erfar blames Babur, while Babur’s earlier warning makes Zak suspect both men. Estera suggests setting a trap. Zak tells each suspect a different location for a second flower; the ambush appears at the place he gave Erfar. With Rivar’s support he confronts and imprisons the elder. An expedition report recovered from the abandoned foreign camp becomes leverage: Erfar translates its account of a concealed tunnel and its opening lever. He later escapes custody. Estera recalls that he originally arrived as an adult stranger, leaving his real purpose unresolved. Babur welcomes the exposure and says that the villagers feared Erfar rather than loved him. Estera introduces a lost Khadaganian [[character/clerk|official]], who promises that his expedition can help Zak leave Gipath. Meeting [[character/hwleader]] instead leads to imprisonment and demands for information about a meteorite. Zak plays the ignorant swineherd, but the commander threatens torture. [[character/oliz]] offers escape on the condition that Zak later visit his home. Zak gives his word, receives the Ancient Claw for the traps on the approach and escapes. The Hermit explains that he had intended to negotiate with the armoured humans but changed his mind after seeing their treatment of Zak. Keeping the promise establishes trust where the expedition failed to do so. The Hermit offers more than directions. He gives Zak an object resembling a horn or shell, hoping it will help him survive, although he cannot explain how a human should use it. His advice about treasure is less benevolent. During their negotiations he points Zak toward the southern lizard islands and says their gold will be his. Zak can follow that lead, only to find hostile owners who pursue the intruder. When confronted, the Hermit calls the misleading invitation a joke, imitating the humour Zak had used with him. Zak makes clear that he does not find the experience amusing. The Hermit needs the water diverted by the orcs restored. Zak raises their dam and blocks the diversion canal; in return the lizard locates the magician in a ravine in the Remote Mountains. This information joins the tunnel instructions from the Khadaganian report. Zak passes the ancient defences and reaches [[character/rick]]. Tka-Rik explains that his dragonet has watched Zak since his unusual arrival. Bound to Gipath by his duty as its Great Magician, he offers help with Zak’s memory in exchange for bringing him two surviving young Joons. The first journey will be to Ingos to find the girl. Zak must leave his Gipath companions behind. Tka-Rik supplies an amulet for the return journey, but warns that it will work only once the girl has been found; his dragonet will travel with Zak. Before leaving Gipath, Zak can finish the separate search for Airy, who set out to find the magician herself and impress him. Estera’s vision points to a goblin prison, where Zak finds her granddaughter’s potion bottle and a note leading to [[character/orcc]]. The orc chief intends to give Airy to a frightening armoured human he calls a Demon. Zak offers to remove this threat instead. Shei-Var first demands proof of his strength against the ogre brothers, whose wealth also threatens the chief’s influence. Once Zak defeats the Demon, Shei-Var honours his promise and sends Airy home. The rescue ends with Estera’s gratitude and Airy’s distress that Zak still regards her as a child. On [[allod/ingos]], Zak first crosses the hostile countryside to reach the city. [[character/kapitan]] tells him about the missing young woman known locally as the Princess and the reward offered for finding her. Governor [[character/huber]] takes a personal interest in her, while [[character/magess]] discourages the search. The hunter [[character/trapper]] provides a concrete lead: another investigator, the Snoop from the capital, had followed the same trail before disappearing east of the city. Finding his body changes the search for a missing girl into an investigation of murder. The arrow in the Snoop’s body appears to implicate the Woodsfolk. Sver explains that their markings identify a clan, while the governor discovers that the case containing similar arrows has been stolen from his collection. Two lines of inquiry now run alongside each other: the stolen collection and the Woodsfolk’s testimony. To approach [[character/ycf]], Zak first returns the Green Clan’s Sacred Flower after rescuing its keeper from the White Clan. Grey Leaf then asks for help with the kidnapped elder Khabburu and his captor. The clan ultimately identifies the murder arrow as a false attribution, even refusing to blame its enemies for it. When the clan moves, Zak receives access to its hidden route and new home. [[character/shopper]] first lets Baldie’s name slip while boasting that mechanical traps are better than magical ones, then denies knowing anything useful. Tilvar mentions the merchant’s mechanical grinder and the disruption caused when it breaks. Sver knows how to turn these leads into pressure. Zak first delivers the hunter’s furs to a buyer outside the merchant’s monopoly. Sver then reveals Karansul’s hidden trade and unpaid taxes, pointing to the foreman’s accounts; he also recommends [[character/mthief]] as a teacher. With the accounts as leverage, Zak learns where to find [[character/vor]], called Baldie, and secures a meeting. Evidence from the stolen collection makes the thief confess: he killed the Snoop, planted the Woodsfolk arrow and worked for a cloaked employer who knew how to evade the governor’s magical traps. At the Green Clan’s new home, Grey Leaf describes the supposed man in grey as a white-haired woman. Zak identifies Diera, whose own traps protected the stolen collection. Her urgent warnings against the abandoned mines reinforce his suspicion. Tilvar explains that the governor holds the key. Karansul suggests winning it with a gold nugget and gives access to a dangerous pit, concealing the tigers that drove out its workers; Sver warns Zak of the trap. Zak obtains the nugget and presents it to the collector-governor as a business prospect. Valrasian releases the mine key, opening the way past Diera’s mercenaries. The former punishment cell is empty. Zak follows the trail deeper into the Forbidden Catacombs until he finds [[character/deva]], who first mistakes him for another captor. She has escaped the mercenaries and found protection through the ancient treaty between Joons and Wormheads. She rejects the nickname Princess and explains that Diera imprisoned her out of jealousy over the governor. Zak falls in love with her, but she remains faithful to At-Zako, who drew the Joon Curse away from her. Zak promises to respect that bond. They return to Tka-Rik, and the next mission becomes the search for her missing beloved on Suslanger. Before Zak leaves for Suslanger, Tka-Rik describes the Khadaganian hierarchy, in which even a master is subject to someone above him. Emperor Neseb is himself a powerful magician. Suslanger is a provincial backwater, but that does not make it safe. The old Joon portal provides a route there; informants and imperial attention make open enquiries about the missing Joon dangerous. Zak is captured near the portal on [[allod/suslanger]]. Lieutenant [[character/karh]] presents him to [[character/iz]], who orders him used as live quarry for soldiers seeking promotion. Surviving the run through Death Canyon earns only a return to captivity, not freedom. Kardaur threatens punishment through necromancy if Zak dies too quickly and displeases his superior. The [[character/nalo]] approaches Zak after his ordeal. Enslaved by Kardaur and deprived even of a personal name, she wants his death and knows he will guard the gate that night. She steals the key to Zak’s cage. Her father, a rat hunter who disappeared in the caves, told her of the Wormheads’ temple and the bridges across its lava rivers. She uses that knowledge to explain a route the guards fear to follow. Zak kills Kardaur for the fortress key and escapes toward the cave; releasing the caged spiders can delay pursuit. The Odalisque and Zak part with wishes for each other’s freedom and survival, without a stated account of her later fate. Beyond the caves, [[character/kuzn]] finds Zak and vouches for him before [[character/glav]]. The brotherhood’s leader fears imperial spies and requires the Emperor’s Signet Ring, taken from a cyclops who killed its courier. Possessing such an object compromises the newcomer with the authorities and makes the test more than a feat of strength. After Zak returns, Khatul accepts him as Brother Blondie and offers the refuge as a new home. Zak explains his promise to find At-Zako and return to Gipath. Khatul respects that purpose and asks those who can help to support him; [[character/guru]] can teach him greater dexterity. The Shelter’s inhabitants can ask for help with their own grievances alongside the search for At-Zako. Brother Blacksmith wants the slavedriver brothers Lash-Aga and Whip-Aga killed at the plantations. If Zak carries out the request, the workers raise the alarm instead of helping him. The smith explains that imperial law threatens them with death if they fail to report a stranger, then promises to repay the revenge. Kehel offers a separate commission: destroy a harpy he once experimented on, so rivals cannot claim his work. After its death, he admits that fear of Zak’s strength is what makes him honour the promised reward. Their requests expose different consequences of life under the empire: coerced obedience among the workers, personal revenge among its fugitives, and rivalry among its scholars. [[character/merc10]] supplies the next lead through her own theft. Antiquities she stole from [[character/junofil]] remain hidden near the city, and Zak recovers them to arrange a meeting. Khatul and Brother Blacksmith help choose the secluded trading place, keeping strangers away from the Shelter. Baluddin admits recognising At-Zako as a living Joon and wanting to keep him in his own house. Imperial scholars took the young man away. Later, Taivo summoned the collector to identify those scholars’ mutilated bodies. The missing youth’s trail now leads to the necromancers rather than a living prisoner whom Zak can simply rescue. [[character/nekro]] directs Zak to [[character/oldnekro]], whom Taivo displaced from the imperial laboratory. Kholai wants disgrace for his rival rather than a simple assassination. Zak steals a dead scientist’s head from the laboratory; its disappearance will embarrass Taivo, and Kholai can summon its spirit. The [[character/spirit|scientist]] describes a horror pursuing the red-skinned youth. To conceal him, the scholars changed his appearance and sent him away by teleportation. Kholai interprets the broken testimony and tells Zak to search the ruined mansion for the magical object used in the escape. The fragments Zak finds are beyond Kehel’s ability to interpret: only a Great Magician can identify the destination. Kholai can also give Zak an experimental object to test in combat. He is interested in the result even if the trial kills its user, a further sign of the limits of his concern for his visitor. Khatul asks [[character/zaku]] to help Zak reach the guarded portal. Faceless arranges a cave meeting and explains the keys and stone controls. He then reveals himself as Erfar: born on Suslanger, he went to Gipath seeking the meteorite and manipulated the villagers into searching for it. His earlier plots were attempts to remove Zak, who disrupted that scheme. The reunion is another trap, with guards waiting outside the cave. Zak survives the confrontation and forces a route through the portal’s defences. Activating its two controls finally returns him to Tka-Rik with the amulet fragments. Tka-Rik initially expects Zak to bring the missing Joon with him. Lu-a-Jalla defends the exhausted traveller, and Zak insists that he will continue for her sake even if reunion with At-Zako means losing her. The amulet changes everything: Tka-Rik discovers that its destination was Gipath. Only Zak arrived there in that unusual way. The man he has been seeking is himself, hidden by the Khadaganian transformation spell. Restored as At-Zako, he reassures Tka-Rik and reunites with Lu-a-Jalla. The memories of their earlier flight explain why the return of his identity also brings back the danger of the Curse. If companions have come from Suslanger, Tka-Rik sends them back by a safe route beyond the imperial guards. Their departure does not mean that they have settled on Gipath. The hurried transformation that concealed At-Zako nearly destroyed his memory. Tka-Rik cannot safely repeat it, so hiding as Zak is no longer an answer. He offers another choice: flee again under his temporary protection, or confront the Curse on Gipath. At-Zako chooses to defend his life with Lu-a-Jalla. Tka-Rik supplies ancient Joon equipment and joins him in the catacombs for the final battle. Defeating the Curse completes the campaign.
